candidates.name: Acute Hemorrhagic Leukoencephalitis
support_spans: High-grade fever for 14 days
Progressive weakness on the right side of body for 5 days
Upper motor neuron type right-sided seventh cranial-nerve palsy
Complete hemiplegia
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of high-grade fever, progressive weakness, and upper motor neuron palsy suggest a neurological disorder.

candidates.name: Cerebral Vasculitis
support_spans: Multifocal smooth stenosis of both intracranial internal carotid arteries
Diffuse narrowing of M2 and M3 segment branches of both middle cerebral arteries
candidates.why: The imaging findings of multifocal smooth stenosis and diffuse narrowing of cerebral arteries suggest a vasculitic process.

candidates.name: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
support_spans: High-grade fever for 14 days
Progressive weakness on the right side of body for 5 days
Pleocytosis with slightly increased protein in CSF
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and CSF findings suggest an autoimmune or post-infectious encephalomyelitis.

candidates.name: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
support_spans: Multifocal smooth stenosis of both intracranial internal carotid arteries
Diffuse narrowing of M2 and M3 segment branches of both middle cerebral arteries
candidates.why: The imaging findings suggest a primary vasculitic process affecting the central nervous system.

candidates.name: Multifocal Necrotizing Leukoencephalopathy
support_spans: Multifocal discrete and confluent hypodensities in genu and adjacent body of corpus callosum
Pleocytosis with slightly increased protein in CSF
candidates.why: The imaging and CSF findings suggest a necrotizing leukoencephalopathy, which could be confirmed by brain biopsy or autopsy.

candidates.name: Cerebral Malaria
support_spans: High-grade fever for 14 days
Progressive weakness on the right side of body for 5 days
Multifocal smooth stenosis of both intracranial internal carotid arteries
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings could suggest cerebral malaria, which could be confirmed by blood smear or PCR for Plasmodium species.
